verdict.rationale: Gitleaks is a secret-detection scanner, so verifying detected secrets against the issuing service is a fair question for it. The evidence covers only pattern-based detection: custom rules, composite rules, allowlists, baselines, git/dir/stdin scans and the GitHub Action. Nothing shows it checks whether a finding is a live credential, and allowlists or composite rules are adjacent false-positive controls, not live verification.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can have detected secrets verified against the issuing service so I know which ones are live
